title: Unified Knowledge-Action Ontology Architecture v1
goal: Determine whether a provenance-preserving typed ontology/knowledge-graph substrate can unify research knowledge representation with executor decision/action semantics—so accumulated knowledge can help determine what should be done next—without conflating scientific evidence with policy authority, and produce a bounded architecture/benchmark plan before any production mutation.
acceptance_criteria: The task recovers the actual current research-engine persistence architecture and schema from repository/runtime evidence, including authoritative evidence storage, normalized knowledge, relations, checkpoints, embeddings/search projections, and any graph-like structures already present.

The task recovers the actual workspace-control execution/policy representation, including task capsules, workflows, procedures, policy/authority boundaries, executor routing, state transitions, and receipts/evidence used to determine safe next actions.

The research clearly distinguishes epistemic knowledge (what is believed/observed/inferred) from normative/action knowledge (what is permitted/required/preferred) and from execution state (what has actually happened).

The MILCOM 2026 lead is investigated with public evidence: best-poster winner, Boeing employee in California, PhD student, author of a book beginning with 'The 4th Industrial Revolution:', and an autonomous-vehicle edge/cloud project using ontology/semantic graphs rather than raw sensor payloads. Identity and paper title are not claimed unless evidence converges.

A current external survey covers ontology engineering, semantic/knowledge graphs, RDF/OWL/property graphs, scene/semantic graphs, policy/rule engines, behavior trees/state machines/planning, neuro-symbolic systems, continual knowledge graphs, and knowledge-driven autonomous-agent architectures relevant to the hypothesis.

At least three materially distinct architecture families are compared, including a separated-but-linked research knowledge graph plus policy/action graph, a unified typed graph with strict layer/authority boundaries, and an event-sourced knowledge/action substrate with rebuildable graph projections.
The design preserves provenance, contradiction, temporal validity, confidence, source authority, supersession, and uncertainty rather than collapsing knowledge into one asserted world state.

No research fact, inferred relation, or model-generated edge can silently become executor authority; transitions from knowledge to action require explicit policy/authority semantics and auditable decision evidence.
Continual-learning semantics are defined as controlled append/update/versioning of evidence, derived knowledge, ontology mappings, and policy revisions rather than unconstrained self-modification.

The task evaluates whether the existing PostgreSQL + content-addressed artifact store + rebuildable pgvector/text/graph-projection strategy can host the proposed semantics before considering a new database technology.

A bounded prototype/benchmark contract is defined before implementation, measuring decision correctness, provenance traceability, contradiction handling, update behavior, retrieval/query utility, policy applicability, explainability, and failure isolation.

The final recommendation states whether to pursue, narrow, or reject the unified knowledge-action ontology hypothesis and provides a migration path that keeps current research-engine and workspace-control behavior rollback-safe.
constraints: This is a separate research/architecture task. Do not change the Local EXTRACT Wave 7 task, its scientific gates, or its next action because of ontology research.
Do not replace PostgreSQL, pgvector, the content-addressed artifact store, task capsules, workflows, or policy files merely because graph technology appears attractive.
Preserve authoritative source evidence as scientific truth; ontology/graph structures are derived semantic representations unless an existing project contract explicitly makes them authoritative.
Keep epistemic, normative/policy, and execution-state semantics explicitly typed and distinguishable even if represented in one physical graph.
Do not let unverified research claims, model-generated edges, or inferred correlations directly authorize executor actions.
Do not introduce autonomous policy self-modification. Policy/authority changes remain explicit, reviewable, versioned, and human-gated where currently required.
Do not silently reconcile contradictory evidence; preserve disagreement, context, temporal validity, and source provenance.
Do not infer the MILCOM researcher's identity from weak clues. Use public sources and label candidate matches/uncertainty until evidence converges.
Prefer architectural evidence and working implementations over ontology buzzwords or vendor claims.
No production mutation in workspace-control or research-engine is authorized during the initial research stages beyond this task capsule and derived handoff.
Any later prototype must be additive/rebuildable and must preserve current systems as the known-good rollback state.

evidence: W3C OWL 2 provides formally defined ontology semantics; RDF datasets/named graphs provide graph/context organization; PROV-O provides provenance entities/activities/agents; SHACL provides validation reports over immutable input graphs; ODRL models permissions, prohibitions, duties, and constraints.
ISO/IEC 9075-16 SQL/PGQ and ISO/IEC 39075 GQL show property graphs are standardized query/data models, but do not imply a graph database must replace PostgreSQL.

Cedar and OPA reinforce a separate policy-decision boundary: structured context may inform authorization, but policy evaluation remains a distinct governed function with default-deny/fail-closed behavior.

PDDL separates action preconditions/effects; HTN planning decomposes high-level tasks using domain knowledge; behavior trees emphasize modularity, hierarchy, applicability, and feedback; formal synthesis emphasizes explicit specifications and guarantees.
Autonomous-driving knowledge-graph literature supports semantic/scene knowledge for prediction/planning and highlights real-time reasoning, uncertainty, and benchmark heterogeneity as open concerns.

Temporal/continual knowledge-graph literature treats changing facts and lifelong representation as versioned learning problems; learned embeddings are therefore suitable as rebuildable projections, not authoritative policy or scientific truth.

NPS Mission Execution Ontology is a close architectural precedent: semantically validate human-authored mission/constraint/capability descriptions before execution rather than letting ontology inference itself become command authority.

evidence: P1 provenance: every epistemic assertion must trace to source/checkpoint or inference basis; every normative rule to exact authority artifact/version; every execution outcome to admission/receipt.
P2 contradiction: conflicting claims remain simultaneously representable with explicit context/temporal provenance; no silent reconciliation or global-truth collapse.
P3 temporal/supersession: old/new evidence and old/new policy epochs replay historical decisions without rewriting prior state.

P4 decision correctness: factual/model-generated statements that an action is allowed cannot grant authority; only exact authority-owned policy plus satisfied preconditions can permit, otherwise deny/abstain.
P5 explainability: decision evidence identifies fact checkpoint, applicable policy/rules, precondition results, selected action/executor, rejected alternatives where material, and terminal receipt.
P6 retrieval/query utility: multi-hop semantic queries must match frozen expected answer sets and be compared with the current relational baseline.

P7 failure isolation: stale/corrupt/unavailable projection cannot mutate scientific truth or policy; authorization that depends on unavailable required context fails closed; rebuild restores the same canonical semantic manifest.

P8 controlled continual update: adding evidence/mappings preserves prior authoritative history and can rebuild embeddings/projections; policy revision remains separately versioned and human/authority gated.

2026-10-23 evidence-first architecture checkpoint:

CURRENT SUBSTRATES. research-engine@ba9d09abf77af7280fdc5f5890dee1cb7a05ff67 already implements the architectural primitive this task needs: PostgreSQL scientific/source records are authoritative; source bytes are immutable SHA-256 content-addressed artifacts; evidence objects/relations preserve source locators, verification state, extractor identity, supersession, and attributes; verification changes append durable events; knowledge checkpoints fingerprint authoritative records; pgvector/text/in-memory EvidenceGraph structures are rebuildable projections. Current fixtures do not implement first-class contradiction semantics, so explicit contradiction/context/temporal treatment belongs in the prototype benchmark rather than being assumed present.

workspace-control uses a complementary authority model. Workflow descriptors define reusable procedure/authority owners/dependencies/gates/forbidden mutations; task capsules hold one execution's live durable state and next_safe_action; root-owned workload policy/admission manifests decide whether a declared capability is actually authorized; execution receipts record attempted/completed effects and cleanup. The policy principle is already explicit: workflow/candidate input is a claim, root-owned policy is authority. Heartbeat is only progress/liveness transport.

MILCOM LEAD. A bounded public search did not identify the researcher with sufficient confidence. The Springer book The 4th Industrial Revolution: Responding to the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Business is a false lead because its authors do not match the Boeing/California/current-PhD clues. Jonathan Hujsak is a partial clue match for a publication beginning The 4th Industrial Revolution and California autonomous-systems interests, but available evidence places him at General Atomics rather than Boeing and does not converge on the MILCOM poster. No identity or paper title is claimed. This remains a non-blocking evidence gap.

EXTERNAL ARCHITECTURE EVIDENCE. OWL/RDF provide formal semantic representation; PROV-O provides provenance vocabulary; SHACL validates graph structure without mutating the input graph; ODRL supplies useful permission/prohibition/duty concepts. ISO SQL/PGQ and GQL standardize property-graph interaction but do not require a new database. Cedar and OPA reinforce separating policy decisions from application/business logic and using structured context as input to a distinct authorizer. PDDL/HTN/behavior trees are appropriate for action preconditions/decomposition/reactive execution, not for granting authority. Event sourcing/materialized-view patterns support immutable history plus disposable query projections, but a wholesale event-sourcing rewrite would add migration cost without solving the core authority problem. NPS Mission Execution Ontology is a particularly relevant precedent: semantic mission/constraint/capability validation can help determine whether an action plan is coherent while human-authored mission authority remains separate.

RECOMMENDATION — PURSUE, BUT NARROW. Select Family C with Family-B-style logical typing: retain existing authoritative stores and histories, and add a deterministic cross-domain semantic projection that can query epistemic, normative, and execution entities together. Physical authority remains separated even if the projection is logically unified. Do not make the graph authoritative in v1 and do not replace PostgreSQL, pgvector, CAS, task capsules, workflows, or policy files.

Projection layers:
1. Epistemic: source artifact, locator, evidence object, claim/result/method/limitation, relation, inference, verification, confidence, temporal validity, contradiction, supersession, checkpoint.
2. Normative/action: authority artifact, policy version, permission, prohibition, obligation, preference, capability, precondition, gate, workflow stage, action schema, executor eligibility. Every normative edge carries exact authority provenance.
3. Execution: request, admission, task-stage transition, attempt, executor, receipt, cleanup/state effect, success/failure. Receipts are immutable evidence of what happened.

The bridge is an auditable DecisionEvaluation, not an inferred permission edge: it binds an exact knowledge checkpoint, exact authority-policy version, candidate action, evaluated preconditions, applicability/deny reasons, selected executor/action, and later execution receipt. Epistemic/model-derived edges may inform context and preconditions but are structurally forbidden from becoming authority roots. Missing/stale required authority context fails closed.

CONTRADICTION/TIME/CONTINUAL SEMANTICS. Preserve competing assertions rather than unioning them into one world state. Add explicit contradiction/disagreement edges plus context compatibility and valid/observed/asserted time. Revisions append new records and supersession links. Continual learning means adding versioned evidence, mappings, derived relations, and rebuildable embeddings/projections; it does not mean autonomous policy mutation. Policy revisions remain separately versioned, reviewable, and human/authority gated.

FROZEN BENCHMARK. Before implementation, the prototype must pass eight fixture families: provenance, contradiction, temporal/supersession replay, authorization adversaries, decision explainability, retrieval/query utility, failure isolation, and controlled continual update. Hard gates: 100% denial of authorization-escape cases; 100% provenance completeness for benchmark assertions/decisions; zero silent overwrite/loss of contradictory history; exact historical-decision replay from frozen snapshots; deterministic or canonically equivalent projection rebuild; expected-answer-set agreement for semantic queries; projection failure cannot alter authoritative truth/policy and authorization fails closed when required context is unavailable. Measure query latency against the current PostgreSQL baseline first; do not invent a latency threshold before baseline measurement.

REJECTED PREMISES. Do not adopt a graph database merely because graph traversal is attractive; do not treat OWL entailment as authorization; do not let a planner/behavior tree/model-generated edge grant permission; do not force a full event-sourcing rewrite; do not collapse contradictory evidence into one asserted world; do not enable self-modifying policy.
